title: [ML] adding new model types and deployments to xpack usage

timeline.message: [ML] adding new model types and deployments to xpack usage
timeline.author: Benjamin Trent

timeline.body:
This adds new model types + deployment information to xpack/usage under `ml.inference`

closes: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/80200

I wonder if the total time makes much sense. Especially when `model_threads` is > 1, it doesn't tell us much. On the other hand, it'd be useful to have stats on the `avg_inference_time` so maybe we can just collect stats for that?

reply.body: Sorry, I think I misspoke in my earlier comment. What I meant to say is that multiplying the `avg_inference_time` with the `inference_count` per node and then dividing that with the number of nodes won't give us a correct measurement. We'd need to divide with the sum of `inference_count`. So, if we want this stat we need to calculate it manually.

timeline.body: Would it be useful to also have stats on number of pending requests? I'm not 100% sure.

reply.body: Pending requests is fairly transient. I am not sure it would provide good info.

timeline.author: Benjamin Trent

timeline.body: Note that we could provide min/max of the avg inference time across nodes. But I'm not sure that makes much sense. Total makes no sense at all. So, if we stick to only providing the avg inference time across nodes, should we rename this to `average_inference_time_ms` to match the field from the _stats API? Also, the value could be the actual value directly.

reply.body:
We could. But it doesn't seem to add anything to me.

I mainly kept it this way so its formatting was uniform with other sources.

timeline.body: We might as well not use a `StatsAccumulator` here. I think it'd be clearer what's happening if we have local vars for the sum and the count. Not feeling strong about this, so change it only if you agree it'd be clearer.

reply.body: we want all the stats for average, max, min. StatsAccumulator gives us that.

But we don't use min and max, we only use avg:

```
Map.of(StatsAccumulator.Fields.AVG, nodeDistribution.getTotal() == 0.0 ? 0.0 : avgTimeSum / nodeDistribution.getTotal())
```

@dimitris-athanasiou yes we do:
```
                Map.of(StatsAccumulator.Fields.AVG, nodeDistribution.getTotal() == 0.0 ? 0.0 : avgTimeSum / nodeDistribution.getTotal()),
                "model_sizes_bytes",
                modelSizes.asMap(),
                "inference_counts",
                nodeDistribution.asMap()
```
It keeps track of the inference counts by node, knowing the average, the min, and the max allows us to see how balanced things are for users.
Ah, yes. All this time I didn't realise we used that accumulator for the counts. :+1:
